<section class="usage">

### Usage

```c
#include "stdlib/stats/base/ndarray/sstdevch.h"
```

#### stdlib_stats_sstdevch( arrays )

Computes the standard deviation of a one-dimensional single-precision floating-point ndarray using a one-pass trial mean algorithm.

```c
#include "stdlib/ndarray/ctor.h"
#include "stdlib/ndarray/dtypes.h"
#include "stdlib/ndarray/index_modes.h"
#include "stdlib/ndarray/orders.h"
#include "stdlib/ndarray/base/bytes_per_element.h"
#include <stdint.h>

// Create an input ndarray:
const float xbuf[] = { 1.0f, 2.0f, 3.0f, 4.0f };
int64_t xshape[] = { 4 };
int64_t xstrides[] = { STDLIB_NDARRAY_FLOAT32_BYTES_PER_ELEMENT };
int8_t submodes[] = { STDLIB_NDARRAY_INDEX_ERROR };
struct ndarray *x = stdlib_ndarray_allocate( STDLIB_NDARRAY_FLOAT32, (uint8_t *)xbuf, 1, xshape, xstrides, 0, STDLIB_NDARRAY_ROW_MAJOR, STDLIB_NDARRAY_INDEX_ERROR, 1, submodes );

// Create a zero-dimensional ndarray specifying the degrees of freedom adjustment:
const float cbuf[] = { 1.0f };
int64_t *cshape = NULL;
int64_t cstrides[] = { 0 };
struct ndarray *correction = stdlib_ndarray_allocate( STDLIB_NDARRAY_FLOAT32, (uint8_t *)cbuf, 0, cshape, cstrides, 0, STDLIB_NDARRAY_ROW_MAJOR, STDLIB_NDARRAY_INDEX_ERROR, 0, submodes );

// Compute the standard deviation:
const struct ndarray *arrays[] = { x, correction };
float v = stdlib_stats_sstdevch( arrays );
// returns ~2.0817

// Free allocated memory:
stdlib_ndarray_free( x );
stdlib_ndarray_free( correction );
```

The function accepts the following arguments:

-   **arrays**: `[in] struct ndarray**` list containing the following ndarrays: a one-dimensional input ndarray and a zero-dimensional ndarray specifying the degrees of freedom adjustment.

```c
float stdlib_stats_sstdevch( const struct ndarray *arrays[] );
```

</section>

<section class="examples">

### Examples

```c
#include "stdlib/stats/base/ndarray/sstdevch.h"
#include "stdlib/ndarray/ctor.h"
#include "stdlib/ndarray/dtypes.h"
#include "stdlib/ndarray/index_modes.h"
#include "stdlib/ndarray/orders.h"
#include "stdlib/ndarray/base/bytes_per_element.h"
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <stdio.h>

int main( void ) {
    // Create a data buffer:
    const float xbuf[] = { 1.0f, 2.0f, 3.0f, 4.0f, 5.0f, 6.0f, 7.0f, 8.0f };

    // Specify the number of array dimensions:
    const int64_t ndims = 1;

    // Specify the array shape:
    int64_t shape[] = { 4 };

    // Specify the array strides:
    int64_t strides[] = { 2*STDLIB_NDARRAY_FLOAT32_BYTES_PER_ELEMENT };

    // Specify the byte offset:
    const int64_t offset = 0;

    // Specify the array order:
    const enum STDLIB_NDARRAY_ORDER order = STDLIB_NDARRAY_ROW_MAJOR;

    // Specify the index mode:
    const enum STDLIB_NDARRAY_INDEX_MODE imode = STDLIB_NDARRAY_INDEX_ERROR;

    // Specify the subscript index modes:
    int8_t submodes[] = { STDLIB_NDARRAY_INDEX_ERROR };
    const int64_t nsubmodes = 1;

    // Create an input ndarray:
    struct ndarray *x = stdlib_ndarray_allocate( STDLIB_NDARRAY_FLOAT32, (uint8_t *)xbuf, ndims, shape, strides, offset, order, imode, nsubmodes, submodes );
    if ( x == NULL ) {
        fprintf( stderr, "Error allocating memory.\n" );
        exit( 1 );
    }

    // Create a zero-dimensional ndarray specifying the degrees of freedom adjustment:
    const float cbuf[] = { 1.0f };
    int64_t *cshape = NULL;
    int64_t cstrides[] = { 0 };
    struct ndarray *correction = stdlib_ndarray_allocate( STDLIB_NDARRAY_FLOAT32, (uint8_t *)cbuf, 0, cshape, cstrides, offset, order, imode, 0, submodes );
    if ( correction == NULL ) {
        fprintf( stderr, "Error allocating memory.\n" );
        exit( 1 );
    }

    // Define a list of ndarrays:
    const struct ndarray *arrays[] = { x, correction };

    // Compute the standard deviation:
    float v = stdlib_stats_sstdevch( arrays );

    // Print the result:
    printf( "stdev: %f\n", v );

    // Free allocated memory:
    stdlib_ndarray_free( x );
    stdlib_ndarray_free( correction );
}
```

</section>
